triage.guide.arrest.body: The clock ran out and the heart stopped. What is left is a window somebody else holds open by hand. Compressions do not restart anything - they buy the time for somebody to arrive with the kit, every round buys less than the last, and every round is another go at the ribs.
triage.guide.blacked.body: A part at zero. It refuses ordinary healing, and every limb in this state drags the chest down until somebody opens it up.
triage.guide.bleeding.body: Blood is leaving the body, not just the limb. A light bleed closes on its own; a heavy one never does. While it runs the volume falls, and everything else falls with it.
triage.guide.blood_loss.body: What is left once the bleeding is stopped. It comes back slowly, and only with food in you - resting is worth double and sleeping four times. A drip is the fast way, and it refuses while anything is still open.
triage.guide.allergy.body:
Some bodies arrive with one, and most of them are food. Seven of the ten are things you eat - fish, wheat, egg, milk, honey, mushrooms, berries - and three are things out of your own bag: the antibiotics, the morphine, or the anaesthetic. You are told your own on the day you get it.

Eat the wrong thing and your throat starts closing. Nothing warns you and nothing refuses the click, because that is how it happens: bread is what you eat when you are hurt, when you are bored, and when you are running away from something. Give the wrong drug to somebody who has one and the same thing happens to them, and the dose is spent either way - it is not a refusal, it is a treatment that went in and did the wrong thing.

The answer to all of it is the same needle the mod has always kept for exactly this.

So ask. A conscious patient tells you what they cannot have, in the same breath as where it hurts. A patient on the floor tells you nothing, which is why people who cannot afford that conversation to fail wear the sentence on their wrist: stamp a bracelet with your own and anybody who looks at you reads it, talking or not.
triage.guide.graft: The arm is on the floor
triage.guide.graft.body:
A limb that comes off lands next to you, and for a few minutes it is worth sewing back on.

What decides that is not the surgery. It is how long it has been off and how cold it was kept: warm in a pocket it is finished in five minutes, and in water or snow it keeps three times as long. That is the real advice, and it is why a severed hand travels to hospital on ice.

It comes back worse than it was - weak, stiff, and dirty, because it has been on the floor - and it comes back. Which is the whole trade, and everybody who has the choice takes it over a hook.

A limb that was already dead when it came off is meat. The item still drops and still says so.
triage.guide.parasites.body:
From what was eaten, and the slowest thing in this mod by a long way.

They do not burn, they open nothing and they will not kill you this afternoon. They take: they eat before you do and they drink off the blood while they are there, so what you get is hungry, short and tired for as long as you leave it.

They do not pass on their own - nothing about a parasite is self-limiting - and a bottle of antibiotics does nothing whatever for them. What answers them is the other card, which answers nothing else.
triage.guide.burn.body:
Three kinds, and which one you have decides everything else. Red heals itself and wants nothing. Blistered is the most painful of the three and wants a salve. Through the skin will not close at all, and no salve will reach it.

The worst of the three does not hurt. The nerve endings that would have done the hurting are part of what burnt, so the patch somebody is screaming about is the one that is going to be fine, and the quiet patch beside it is the one that needs a knife. That is why a burn is pressed on rather than looked at.

And it is not over when the fire is out. Heat sitting in tissue goes on cooking it for about half a minute, and a burn that was superficial when the flames went out can be through the skin a minute later. Water, in that window, stops it where it is and can talk it back a step. Snow and ice do the opposite and take it deeper.

What kills is the size rather than the depth. Add up what is burnt past the skin - head nine, each arm nine, each leg eighteen, chest and belly eighteen apiece - and past about fifteen percent of somebody, fluid starts going out through their own surface faster than they can spare it. That is a bag of saline, and it is the reason to hurry.
triage.guide.carry.body: Shift and right-click with an empty hand picks somebody up. Your hands are full, you move at half speed, and their clock runs at half pace while you do. Right-click sets them down in front of you.
triage.guide.concussion.body: It does not damage the body, it damages the readout: the bars go coarse and the numbers drift. A concussed medic reads somebody else's chart as badly as their own. It wears off.
triage.guide.crack.body: Not broken yet. Left alone it knits; leaned on - sprinted on, hit again - it becomes the thing a splint is actually for.
triage.guide.downed.body: An emptied head or chest is the floor and a clock, not a death. You cannot move, cannot fight, cannot save yourself. A dressing holds the clock, a surgical kit stands you up - and holding the airway open is the part that needs nothing at all. An unattended airway closes in twenty seconds and doubles the clock.
triage.guide.fracture.body: It never knits on its own. You can run on a broken leg - it charges you for it. Ribs break in numbers, and every one of them is its own pass with a splint.
triage.guide.hypothermia.body: Almost nothing on its own, except that blood will not clot: a light cut that would have closed in a minute simply keeps running. Warmth and dry ground clear it, and firelight clears it twice as fast.
triage.guide.illness.body: A cold, poisoning, fever, sepsis. One course of antibiotics is the only thing that touches any of them, and it is aimed at the body rather than at a limb.
triage.guide.infection.body: An open wound nobody cleaned out. Left alone it goes to fever and then to sepsis, and past that point a dressing is not the answer any more.
triage.guide.nothing: Nothing in the box treats this.
triage.guide.pain.body: Painkillers heal nothing at all - they hide the penalties while the damage goes on piling up. Each further course inside the window is shorter than the last, and the tolerance only falls once the previous dose is out of you.
triage.guide.pneumo.body: The one injury with nothing to see - nothing bleeds, nothing is bent - and the only one that speeds up the longer it waits. It happens only after ribs have gone, which is what makes splinting a cracked chest worth it.
triage.guide.shock.body: From a third of the volume gone, or from two parts taken at once. It halves what blood you make back and runs the downed clock half as fast again. It lifts when nothing is open, the volume is back, and you hold still - and standing up starts the count again.
triage.guide.skull.body: You do not strap a stick to somebody's back. These two go to the surgical kit, which is the most expensive thing in the box, and that is the right way round.
triage.guide.tags.body: Four colours, written onto somebody from their chart and visible to everybody on their nameplate. The mod never works out which one is correct - the person looking decides, and they are wrong exactly as often as they are.

triage.guide.artery.body: Not a worse cut - a different injury. It goes in time with the heart, it is brighter than the rest, and it does not clot, ever. A dressing over one soaks through and keeps soaking. There are two answers and you already have both: a hand pushed hard into it, or a strap above it. Nothing else works, and the count is in tens of seconds.

triage.guide.faint.body: Not the same as going down. Being downed is a clock counting towards a grave; this is a body deciding it cannot keep the head supplied while standing up, so it stops standing up - which fixes it. Seven seconds later you are fine and nothing needs treating. What it costs is the seven seconds and wherever you happened to be: on a ledge, in water, or in front of something that was already swinging. Volume does it, pain on its own does it, and getting up quickly makes it likelier.

Running on it does not start you over - it puts time back on, every second of it, and it takes longer again the next time you do it. When the clock ends the splint comes off by itself and the bone is done.
triage.guide.sever.body: An edge, swung hard, into a limb - mostly one that has already been beaten past being a limb. A fist does not do this and neither does an arrow. What it leaves is the ragged stump a blast leaves: open, unstrapped, and the arm on the ground beside you with a clock on it.
triage.msg.knit_scar: %1$s has knitted. Broken here %2$d time(s) now.
triage.guide.scar.body: The first thing in this mod a body keeps. Skin that has been opened and closed is not skin any more: there is less blood going through it, which is exactly why the next infection settles in the place the last one did. A bone that has knitted is not weak - but it is where the next fall lands, because whatever broke it is the thing you keep doing. Only dying clears any of it.
triage.guide.ache.body: An old break knows when it is going to rain, and knows it indoors, because what it answers to is the pressure rather than getting wet. Cold does it too. It costs nothing, it heals nothing and nothing treats it - it is the one thing in this mod that is only a person telling you about their body.

triage.guide.stiff.body: A deep burn closes by pulling its own edges together, a wound closes tight, and a limb sewn back on never straightens the way it did. A stiff arm is not a weak arm - it is one that does not go where it is put, so what it costs is the quality of anything done with it. Unlike the scar underneath it, this can be worked back down.
triage.guide.stretch.body: Take the joint out to the edge of what it will do and hold it there. Short of the edge nothing loosens - being gentle with a contracture is how people keep one for life. Past the edge something tears and it is tighter tomorrow. The edge is not drawn anywhere, because the only thing that knows where it is, is the person whose arm it is: watch the face. One session per limb per day, and doing it to yourself is worth half, because you stop at your own pain.

triage.guide.sight.body: A body in trouble says so to the person inside it before it says anything to a chart. Volume going closes the edges in and takes the colour out of what is left, and the whole picture dims and comes back on your own pulse - so a screen that has started beating quickly is a reading nobody had to take. A hit head will not hold the horizon still. Fever washes the room warm; cold goes pale and shivers. All of it can be turned down or off in the client settings, and none of it changes what is happening to you.

triage.guide.displaced.body:
A bone can break and stay where it was, or the ends can move. The second one is what people picture when they hear the word, and you do not need a chart for it: the limb is the wrong shape, and everyone in the clearing can see it.

It matters because a splint is no longer the whole answer. Strap a stick to a bone that is out of line and you have held it exactly where it should not be - and in a week that is permanent. Something has to pull it straight first.
triage.guide.set.body:
Bare hands, three moves, in order. Pull along the bone and away from the body until the ends can pass each other - not enough and they grind, too much and something between them tears. Hold that pull and bring the far half back under the near one. Then let it down slowly: the ends seat as the pull comes off, and letting go all at once drops them together however they were lying.

It is the most painful thing in this mod, it is the only treatment the room can hear, and the noise brings whatever is out there. A patient who is under, or far enough into the morphine, makes no noise at all - which is the first reason to carry the mask that has nothing to do with quality.
triage.guide.open_bone.body:
The worst of the three, and the only one that is also a wound. It bleeds, it cannot close while there is bone in the way, and it is the fastest road to infection here - the inside of a leg has been introduced to the floor.

Nothing is set and no splint goes on. It wants a surgeon, to clean it out and close it, and what is left afterwards is an ordinary displaced fracture: hands, then a stick, then a week.
triage.guide.crooked.body:
A bone left out of line knits out of line. The limb keeps the angle, it is worth less than it was for good, and it aches on the weather louder than a straight one ever did.

There is one way out and it is the real one: a surgeon breaks it again, on purpose, so that this time somebody can set it straight. It is the only treatment in this mod that is the injury.

triage.guide.clot.body:
The one injury here that nothing does to you. Blood that is not moving sets - and what stops it moving is a strap, a splint, a broken leg, and an hour spent lying on the floor waiting for somebody to come. Which makes it the first thing in this mod caused by treatment: the tourniquet that saved the limb and the stillness that let it work.

The leg is not the danger. It swells, it is warm, it aches, and that is all it will ever do - there is nothing to see and nothing to put a hand on, and the only way the mod hands it over is by asking the patient where it hurts.

What it is waiting for is you to stand up. Walking is the prevention and walking is the trigger, and there is no version of this where that is not true.
triage.guide.embolism.body:
A clot that has been sitting in a still limb goes when the limb starts working, and it does not stop in the leg. What arrives in the chest is something solid where the air was going: the breathing goes first, the heart follows it up, and the chest comes apart faster than anything in this mod except an artery.

No bandage, no drip, no course of anything. One drug breaks it up rather than treating the damage, and it has about a minute and a half to be found in somebody's bag. Carry one if anybody in your group has been off their feet.
triage.guide.film.body:
The one thing in this mod that looks inside somebody, and the only reading with no opinion in it. It does not ask the patient anything, it cannot be talked out of an answer by morphine or a concussion or the patient being unconscious, and it does not care how steady your hands are. What is on the film is what is in the arm.

It shows bone - sound, cracked, broken, out of line, healed crooked, including the cracks nobody can feel and the ribs and skulls that have no outside to look at - and metal, which is every fragment still in somebody, counted.

And it shows nothing else at all. No bleeding, no infection, no clot, no torn spleen. A film of a man dying of a ruptured organ is a clean film. Anybody who learns to trust the picture instead of their hands will kill somebody with it.

The machine is heavy and stays where you built it, which is the trade: everything else a medic owns travels, and finding out what is really broken means bringing the patient to the machine.
triage.guide.notes.body:
The chart used to print a live pulse for anybody it was opened over - walk up to a stranger and the screen handed you a heart rate nobody had ever felt for. That made taking one worth nothing, and it made the second medic to arrive repeat everything the first had already done.

Readings are written down now. A pulse taken is a pulse on the notes, with the name of whoever took it and how long ago; a temperature measured with the instrument is the figure, not the word; a film leaves a line saying a picture exists. Until somebody has done it, the line is empty.

And they go stale. A pulse from four minutes ago is a fact about four minutes ago, and on a patient who is bleeding that is the difference between a number and a lie - so the chart keeps the figure and says how old it is, which is what a real one does.
triage.guide.operations.body:
The surgical kit used to be one item, one screen and one game for six different jobs. A limb beaten to nothing, a spleen with a hole in it, a burn that had to be cut off, a skull that had to be opened, a leg with the bone outside it and a bone that healed in the wrong shape were all "use the surgical kit", and all of them were the same two minutes of clamping bleeders.

They are six now, and the kit picks the one the part is actually asking for, worst first. A leg with the bone outside it and a burn on the same leg is two operations, because it is two operations.
triage.guide.op_irrigate.body:
For a fracture that has been outside. Not a repair - the bone is still broken and still out of line when you have finished - but the end of a race: an open fracture is the inside of a leg introduced to whatever it landed on.

The solution to pollution is dilution. Not picking grit out one piece at a time: washing it out, in quantity, with one bottle and no second one. Work from the middle outwards and drive it over the edge.
triage.guide.op_trephine.body:
For the two bones no splint reaches. A skull and a spine are a box, and what is inside the box is now being squeezed by its own swelling with nowhere to go.

So: a hole. Not on the fracture line and not on a vessel - both are drawn, and both are refused rather than punished. Then through the bone and not a millimetre past it. Nothing tells you where to stop except the bone itself, which gives under the bit when it is nearly through.
triage.guide.op_organ.body:
For what is torn inside. The difference from every other job in this mod is not the stitching - it is that the patient is breathing, and everything under the ribs moves when they do.

The skill is waiting. A chest rises, pauses at the top and at the bottom, and moves again; a needle put in while the surface is travelling does not make a stitch, it makes the tear longer. Nothing on screen says when the pause is. Watch it for a second before you touch anything.
triage.guide.op_excise.body:
For a burn through the skin. What is on the arm is not injured tissue, it is dead tissue: it does not heal, it does not take a salve, and it is where everything that goes wrong afterwards starts.

How do you know when you have reached living skin? It bleeds. Dead tissue is dry and takes the blade without complaint, and the moment a patch answers with blood, that patch is finished - going on from there is cutting a hole in somebody who did not have one.
triage.guide.op_debride.body:
The original operation, and still what the word means when nobody says which. A limb beaten to nothing, opened up, the field cleared so you can see, the vessels that are filling it clamped one at a time, and the whole thing closed again.

It is a fight for the view: the field fills so you cannot see, you swab it clear, and what you find is what was filling it. The patient pays for every second in volume.
triage.guide.op_osteotomy.body:
The only operation here that is the injury, and the only one that is never an emergency. The bone knitted, the patient walked out, and what they walked out with was a limb the wrong shape.

Cut it through where the angle is - along a line somebody stood and thought about, which is the one time in this mod that is true - and then close the wedge squarely. The whole point of the exercise is that the last person to do this left it crooked.
triage.guide.title: What to do
triage.guide.tourniquet.body: It stops the bleeding at once and starts killing the limb: nothing below the strap is fed and nothing below it heals. Keep the arm, or keep the blood.
triage.aid.pull.hint: Costs nothing but a steady hand. Nothing about that wound can be dealt with until it is out
triage.guide.arrow.body: Not extra damage - the damage happened on the way in. It is a wound nobody can deal with while it is there: it will not clot, it will not mend, and a bandage over the top of it is a bandage over an arrow. Pulling it costs nothing but a steady hand, and it is the only thing in the mod that can leave somebody worse off than before you helped: done well it leaves an ordinary cut, jerked out it tears. Waiting for steadier hands is a real plan.
triage.guide.bullet.body:
The same wound an arrow leaves and not the same way out. A round does not stand out of the skin: it is under it, so there is nothing to take hold of and draw back along its own track. The wound has to be opened and the thing picked out, which is forceps work rather than a steady pull - and until it is out the part will not clot, will not mend and cannot be dressed.

A bad cut-out tears more than a bad pull does, because the jaws are working inside tissue that has already been torn once. Done well it leaves an ordinary cut; done badly it leaves a heavy bleed and takes more of the patient with it.

A pistol round and a rifle round do not look the same under the skin, and the table names the calibre before the wound is open - nothing here draws every round as one 9mm.

triage.guide.dead.body: A limb that stopped being fed and has stopped being alive. A tourniquet left on too long does it, and so does something festering that nobody cleaned; you are told out loud with a third of the time left, and the clock runs back down the moment the cause is dealt with. Past that point nothing treats it - no dressing, no medkit, no surgeon. It has no health to heal and it poisons the body it is attached to until it comes off.
triage.guide.missing.body: It is off, and that is the improvement: what a dead limb was costing the chest stops the moment it is removed. Put a tourniquet above the cut before you start - with one there is a stump that clots like any other wound, without one there is an artery open on it that never will. It costs volume and it puts the patient into shock either way. Nothing grows back, and it will still hurt, which is not a bug.
triage.guide.prosthetic.body: A wooden leg or a hook, screwed to a stump that has stopped bleeding. It is not the limb and it does not pretend to be: it hands back about half of one and stops there. That half is the difference between walking and dragging, and it is the only thing at the end of the worst road in the mod.

triage.guide.dressing.body: A bandage is not an event, it is a thing on somebody. While it is fresh it is the best item in the box: nothing under a clean dressing can go bad at all, which is the only preventive thing in the mod. Left on long enough it becomes what is keeping the dirt in - and from that moment the wound can go bad with no waiting at all, which is the commonest way a treated wound turns into an infected one. The answer is another bandage; the dirty one comes off with it. It comes off by itself once there is nothing left underneath worth dressing.

triage.guide.anaesthetic.body: Two things in this mod are done to a patient who is awake and can feel all of it: a surgical kit opening them up, and a saw taking their leg off. Anaesthetic is the difference between an operation and a fight. Operating on somebody conscious caps how well it can possibly go however good the hands are, hurts the part on top of the operation, and can put them into shock from the pain alone. Nobody can put themselves under and then operate - being under is being unable to do anything - so this is the one item whose whole value is what it lets somebody else do properly. The dose is the danger: too much and they stop breathing, which is a state this mod already has an answer to.
triage.tooltip.scissors: Cuts a dressing off. Never touches what is under it
triage.aid.unwrap.hint: Costs nothing but nerve. A fresh one comes away clean; one that has dried on takes the clot with it

triage.guide.unwrap.body: A fresh dressing lifts off. One that has been on a while is stuck to the wound by the thing that was trying to close it, and fingers take that with it - so an old dressing is not only dirty, it is harder to get off. Scissors do not care: the blade against the skin is the blunt one, so the cloth comes off in one piece and the wound never knows. That is the whole reason to carry a pair.
triage.guide.unstrap.body: Free, and nothing goes wrong with it - what happens is simply what the strap was stopping. The wound under it was never closed; that is the whole of what a tourniquet is. Dress it first and the strap comes off with the dressing anyway. Take the strap off first and you are back where you started, with the clock reset.
triage.aid.roll.hint: Costs nothing. On their side an airway holds itself open, which is the only thing holding it
triage.msg.already_rolled: They are already on their side
triage.msg.rolled_back: They have rolled onto their back again
triage.minigame.roll_far: Take the far arm and the far knee
triage.minigame.roll_over: Now roll them towards you, in one movement
triage.minigame.roll_head: Head back, and the top hand under the cheek
triage.guide.roll.body: For somebody on the floor who is still breathing, this is the thing to do, and it is the only treatment in the mod that keeps working after you have gone. On their back the tongue goes the way gravity takes it. On their side it does not, and their airway closes at half the rate - not for twenty seconds, but for as long as nobody moves them. It is done in a particular order: the far arm and the far knee, with the knee as the handle, so the weight comes onto the shoulder and not the face. A blow rolls them back.
triage.msg.reperfusion: The strap is off, and everything that was sitting in that limb is not any more
triage.guide.reperfusion.body: A limb with no blood moving through it does not simply wait. Things build up in it, and the moment the strap comes off they go everywhere - the longer it was on, the more there is. Under a third of the clock it costs nothing at all. Past that it costs the whole body, and it gets worse the longer you leave it, which is the real argument a tourniquet makes: at some point the question stops being when to release it and becomes whether to release it or cut below it. A bandage over the wound releases the strap too, and is charged the same.

triage.guide.organ.body: A hard enough blow to a torso tears something in it, and from that moment the blood is going somewhere nobody can see - into the belly, into the chest, anywhere but out. Nothing appears on the figure. No dressing touches it. It never clots, because there is nothing on the outside for a clot to close, and while it runs the volume falls and does not come back. It is on the chart, so it can be found by reading; it cannot be found by looking, and that is the whole of it. One thing ends it, and it is a surgeon. A bruise inside settles on its own; a tear does not.

triage.guide.wear.body: Nothing made of wood and leather and worn all day stays the shape it was cut to. A socket loosens, a strap stretches, a joint develops play. A worn prosthesis is not a broken one - it never falls off - it is simply less of a leg, down to a bit over half of what it was on the day it was fitted. Fitting a fresh one puts it right, and that is the whole of the maintenance. Losing a limb is not an event somebody gets past; it is a thing they then live with, and living with one is mostly this.

triage.msg.pulse_none: Nothing under your fingers. %s's heart has stopped
triage.msg.pulse_nothing_open: And there is nothing open on them
triage.msg.pulse_nothing_open_self: And there is nothing open on you

triage.guide.pulse.body:
Two fingers on a wrist. It costs nothing, needs no item, works on somebody still standing up, and takes about as long as it takes.

A body losing blood holds its pressure up by driving the heart faster, and it keeps doing that right until it cannot. So a fast thin pulse is the earliest honest sign of a bleed - and a slow one on somebody who ought to be racing is worse news, not better.

Which makes it the only outward sign of the injury that has none. A torn spleen puts nothing on the skin: no drip, no stain, nothing a dressing could go on. If the heart is running hard and there is nothing open on them, the blood went somewhere - and the only place left is inside.

Holding steady on the artery buys the number. A hand that keeps sliding off comes away with 'fast', which is most of what the number was for. Nothing you do here can make anybody worse.
triage.aid.ask.hint: Costs nothing. The only thing that says where - and the only one that can be wrong
triage.msg.ask_muddled: They are not making much sense
triage.msg.ask_muddled_self: You are not sure that is right
triage.msg.ask_silent_self: You could not have answered that
triage.guide.breathing.body:
The one vital you get without touching anybody: you watch, and you have the answer from across the room. It is first in the order everybody is taught - airway, breathing, circulation - because that is the order they kill you in.

Fast and shallow is the tell for a crushed lung, which has never had an outward sign before now. Slow is the other danger, and it is the one you cause: ether and painkillers both press on the drive to breathe, and past a point it reaches nothing.
triage.guide.temperature.body:
The slowest vital and the only one that sees the future. It starts climbing while an infection is still a colour on the chart and long before it is a fever with a name - so somebody who checks every so often catches the thing that kills quietly.

It runs the other way too, and that half is the one people get wrong. Lost blood and cold blood both pull it down, and cold blood does not clot. A casualty going cold is a casualty whose bleeding is about to stop being something a bandage can answer.
triage.guide.ask.body:
Every other reading here is taken off a body. This one comes out of one, and it is the only thing that says where.

A pulse says the blood went somewhere. A conscious person with a torn spleen says which side of their belly it went into. That is how that injury is found in the world: by asking, and believing the answer.

It stops working when they stop being able to talk, which is itself worth knowing. It can be wrong: a rattled head names something that hurts rather than the worst thing, and you are told when the answer came from one.

And painkillers work. A dosed patient reports less than is true - the small complaints go entirely and the big ones come down a grade. You keep the location and lose the urgency, and urgency is what decides who gets treated first.
triage.msg.blast_wave: The air hits you. Nothing shows, and your chest is wrong
triage.msg.pulled_fragment_badly: It tears on the way out: %s
triage.guide.blast.body:
A blast does four things at once, and they are not the same injury.

The wave comes first. Pressure does nothing to muscle - what it destroys is anything with gas in it, lungs first and bowel after - and it leaves no mark at all. Somebody walks away from a blast talking and drowns in their own chest later. The only sign in between is a breathing rate that will not settle.

Then the fragments: several small wounds at once, in whatever was facing it. Same problem an arrow is, same answer.

Then the throw, and then the heat.

And the rule worth knowing: armour stops fragments and does nothing for the wave. Plate is a very good answer to a piece of metal travelling at somebody and no answer at all to the air around it. The hardest casualty to find is the one in full armour with no wound anywhere on them.
triage.msg.deafened: Your ears go, and everything is a long way off
triage.msg.ask_unheard_self: You could not have heard the question
triage.guide.deafness.body:
The injury everybody near an explosion has and nobody counts. No treatment and none needed - it wears off.

What it costs while it lasts is the one sense this mod uses to warn you about yourself. A heartbeat you cannot hear stops telling you how much blood is left, and a pulse has to be counted by eye instead of by ear.

And it costs whoever is treating you. A deafened patient cannot hear the question - so the only channel that says WHERE stops working on exactly the casualty who was closest to the blast, and whose worst injury leaves nothing to see.
triage.minigame.pulse_find_deaf: Two fingers on the wrist. You cannot hear it - watch the trace instead
triage.guide.trail.body:
Everything else here begins with a casualty in front of you. This is the one thing that helps you find one.

Somebody losing blood badly leaves it where they walked. It lasts a few minutes and then it is gone - blood dries, and a world permanently marked by every scratch anybody took would be litter rather than atmosphere.

Fresher is redder. An old trail is brown and harder to follow, which is both true and the reason to hurry.

It cuts both ways. Your own trail leads whoever is looking for you straight to where you are lying - and it leads everybody else there too. A dressing or a strap stops it, which is one more reason to close a wound before you move.
triage.msg.bitten: Something bit you, and it was not well
triage.msg.rabies_shows: It starts. Water turns your stomach and the light hurts
triage.guide.rabies: A bite that was not well
triage.guide.rabies.body:
Every other illness here is a race you can join late. A fever gives you minutes. Sepsis gives you a fight. Both can be answered after they have announced themselves.

This one cannot. It is the only condition in medicine where the treatment works perfectly right up until the first symptom and then does not work at all, ever, for anybody.

So it is silent. It sits there for minutes showing nothing, and a course of antibiotics during that time takes it away completely. There is no sign to wait for and no test to run - only the memory of an animal that bit you and did not behave like an animal.

Which makes it the one reason in this mod to treat somebody who is not ill, and the answer to the question every player asks once: what happens if I wait and see.

triage.guide.theatre.body:
A treatment used to be worth the same wherever it happened and whatever it was done with. A kit opened in a lit room over a table did the same job as one opened face-down in a cave, with the same saw that took somebody else's leg off an hour ago.

The instrument is the famous half. For most of the history of surgery it was the thing that killed people - not the cutting, the carrying: a blade went from one patient into the next and nobody thought anything of it. The saw and the forceps are never spent, and now they are never clean either until somebody cleans them. Scissors are left out of it: nothing here has them opening a wound, so dirt on them would be a chore with nothing at the end of it.

Hold one against a medical table and it comes back clean. Antiseptic does the same for the whole bag in the field, and costs the bottle. That is the trade: the table is free and does not travel.

And the room. A table to work on, light to work by, and a roof - each is worth something, and the table is worth most because it is the one you have to decide to build. An ordinary room leaves a treatment exactly as good as it has always been. A proper theatre is better than that, and a cave floor in the dark is worse.

Water is the field expedient. Leave a dirty instrument lying in a stream and the blood comes off it - which is the part you can see and the part that matters least, and a stream makes its own contribution. It takes one most of the way down and stops short of clean. The last of it still wants a table or a bottle.
triage.guide.mending.body:
Everything here used to end at the moment the treatment did. A surgeon closed somebody up and they stood straight back up and went to work, which is the one thing about surgery nobody who has had any believes.

An operated part is now knitting, and nothing hurries it. There is no item for this and there is not going to be one.

It is not a debuff. Nothing is taken away while it lasts - a mending arm swings exactly as well as it did an hour ago. What it is, is a wound that has not finished being one: sprint on a mending leg, swing or mine with a mending arm, and it comes open again. Then it bleeds, the clock starts over, and somebody has to close it a second time on a person who has already paid for it once.

So the answer is to do nothing, which makes it the only rule here with that answer. And it is the second thing a good theatre buys: a job done well in a proper room knits in half the time of one done badly on a floor.
triage.tooltip.grime_filthy: Filthy - %s patients since it was cleaned
triage.guide.assist.body:
Everything here is easier with somebody else, and for a long time somebody else could do everything except the one thing an assistant actually does, which is hold on.

Crouch next to the patient with an empty hand and you are holding them. Both of those are deliberate - nobody does either by walking past - so the mod never has to guess whether you meant it. One person, not a crowd: a second assistant is not better surgery, it is a room full of people.

It steadies the hands doing the work, wherever they are standing. A pair of hands on a cave floor is worth what a pair of hands is worth.

And it is worth most where there is nothing else. Somebody being operated on awake moves, and held down they move less - which is what an operation was before anaesthetic existed and why every picture of an old operating table has straps on it. It does not stop the pain and it was never meant to. It stops the patient, and it is still worse than the bottle.
triage.guide.fatigue.body:
Two things here are physically heavy, and this mod invented both of them: carrying somebody who cannot walk, and bracing somebody who is being cut into. A medic used to be able to do either forever, which made getting them out first a formality rather than a decision.

It is not a stamina bar. Nothing you normally do builds it - not sprinting, not mining, not fighting. Carrying drains it for as long as you keep walking; holding a patient still costs a lump once, paid when the treatment lands.

A carried body gets heavier as you tire, and at the end your arms give out and put them down wherever you happen to be standing. That is the whole of the pressure: not damage, just the wrong place.

It is the arms doing the work, so the arms decide. A broken, dead or missing one tires up to three times faster - which is what a wounded stretcher-bearer is, without needing a rule of its own.

And tired arms are not steady ones. For a while afterwards everything you treat goes worse, which is the fourth thing that decides an operation after the room, the instrument and the second pair of hands - and the only one of the four that is about the surgeon rather than the arrangements. The answer is to stand still for a moment, which is the same answer mending has.
triage.msg.adrenaline: You do not feel it yet
triage.guide.adrenaline.body:
A wound here used to cost you from the tick it happened: a leg breaks and the limp starts on the same tick, which is the one part of breaking a leg that nobody who has broken one recognises.

For a short while after something bad, you can still run on it. People finish races on stress fractures and walk away from crashes on broken ankles. So a bone going, or a limb going out, buys about twenty-five seconds in which most of the pain is not there.

It hides pain. It does not mend bone. A part that is gone, dead on the body, or beaten past working at all is not helped by this at all - what is missing there is not the will to ignore it, it is the thing that carries the weight. A wooden leg is a mechanical limit, not a painful one, and it stays exactly as good as it was.

And it is not a gift. Your heart is already going, which is the only sign of it anybody else can read - somebody standing on a broken leg saying they are fine, with a pulse of a hundred and twenty, is not fine. Your hands shake, which makes this the worst possible minute to operate on anybody, including yourself. And when it ends it all arrives at once, worse for a while than if it had never happened.

There is no way to ask for it, and no second one until the first has finished being paid for.

triage.guide.score.body:
The first question anybody in pain is asked, anywhere. This mod had the second one - where it hurts - and not this one.

It is the third kind of reading here, and there is now one of each. A pulse is a fact about a body. A temperature is a figure from an instrument. A score is an opinion: it comes out of somebody's mouth and nothing can check it.

So it is wrong in more ways than anything else. Pills and morphine take it down without touching what is wrong. Adrenaline takes it down and sends the bill later. A hit head does not rank things. Shock makes people quiet, and the quietest casualty in the clearing is often the worst one. A burn through the skin says nothing at all.

Which is why you ask. A two out of ten on a heart at a hundred and thirty is not a comfortable patient - it is one somebody has already dosed, and four seconds of asking is cheaper than finding out with a second dose.
triage.aid.touch.hint: How deep it went, by what does not hurt
triage.guide.touch.body:
Free, works on somebody standing up, and the only reading in this mod whose finding is an absence.

Press across the burn. Where it hurts, there is something living under it and it will close. Where pressing does nothing at all, the burn is through the skin - and that patch is the whole reason for doing this, because it is the one a jar of salve is wasted on.

Press in one place and you learn that it is burnt, which you could see. Press across the whole of it and the mod tells you which of the two answers it wants: the jar, or the knife.
triage.guide.smoke: The half of fire that is breathed
triage.guide.smoke.body:
Everything on the outside of somebody is measured in hours. An airway is measured in minutes, and it happens to people who walked out of it looking fine.

It is caught standing in fire or in lava, and nothing about it is on the skin: the tell is the voice going and the breathing getting fast and shallow. No bottle touches it, because this is swelling and not an infection. What it wants is time and air.

Two things make it lethal. Morphine, which presses on the drive to breathe, and a face burnt through - the two together are what closes an airway, and a face burnt through is the oldest warning sign in the trade. What answers a closed airway is a pair of hands, over and over, for as long as it takes.

triage.guide.catching: Colds, and who gave them to you
triage.guide.catching.body:
A sneeze used to be a sound and a line of text addressed to the person sneezing, which is the one audience a sneeze is not for.

It is loud, it is catching, and it hurts. Anybody within four blocks can pick the cold up off you - the first thing in this mod that travels from one player to another. It is a cold and not anything worse on purpose: an illness that spread and also mattered would make standing near a wounded friend the wrong move, and this whole mod is built on standing near wounded friends.

And sneezing with a broken rib costs you, the way anybody who has done it would tell you. If your chest or your belly is still knitting from an operation, a sneeze can open it - which makes it the only way here to come apart without doing anything at all.

A cold left alone in a body that stays cold and wet goes down into the chest after about three minutes. Getting dry and warm is the whole of the answer, which is what getting dry and warm is.
triage.guide.organ_illness.body:
Two illnesses here happen to an organ rather than to a person, and both of them are a middle that was missing.

Pneumonia is a cold that went down into the chest. It bruises both lungs rather than tearing anything, and that is the honest difference between an illness and a wound: there is no hole for a surgeon to find, and opening the chest would achieve nothing at all. It reads on the breathing line and on the forehead, and a course of antibiotics is the only answer. Left long enough it stops being pneumonia.

Peritonitis is a belly full of what was meant to stay in the gut. A torn gut used to roll straight for sepsis - from the wound to the worst thing in the mod in one step, with nothing in between to notice or to act on. Now it says so, runs hot, and eats the belly while somebody decides what to do.

And it is the one illness antibiotics cannot finish. While the gut is still open the cause is still arriving, so a course puts the clock back to the start and buys the time the surgeon needs. The bottle does not end this. The surgeon does.
triage.guide.chill.body:
Three things kill a badly hurt person together, and each one makes the next two worse. This mod already had two of them and did not say so.

Cold blood does not clot. Somebody with hypothermia here never stops bleeding on their own - a light bleed that would have closed by itself simply runs until a dressing goes on it. And losing blood is itself cooling, which is why the temperature reading drops as the volume does.

The third closes the circle: an open body loses heat fast. Opening somebody is what cools them, which is why an operating theatre is kept uncomfortably warm for everybody standing up in it, and why the first virtue of a trauma surgeon is speed.

Where you cut decides the price. A lit room out of the weather costs almost nothing. The open, in the snow, in the rain, at night, costs a great deal - and enough of it is hypothermia, and then nothing they have closes by itself any more.

The answer is not an item and there is not going to be one. Somewhere warm, a fire, a roof, and be quick.

triage.guide.referred: Where it hurts is not where it is
triage.guide.referred.body:
A ruptured spleen hurts at the tip of the left shoulder. It is called Kehr's sign, it is real, and it is how that injury gets found by somebody with no machine to hand. A torn liver does the same on the right. A heart goes down the left arm.

So asking a patient where it hurts can send you to the wrong place, and the patient is not lying and is not confused - they genuinely feel it there. The mod does not mark the answer as suspect, because nothing about the patient is suspect.

What gives it away is everything else. The chart says the shoulder is untouched. The complaint says the shoulder is the worst thing in the body. Those two cannot both be about a shoulder. Add a pulse that is running hard with nothing open on them, and there is only one thing left it can be: the belly is filling up.

It only ever happens when the named place is genuinely unhurt, so the contradiction is always real. If the shoulder were broken too, they would have been complaining about the shoulder anyway, and an answer that could mean either is not a clue.

This is the only thing in the mod that is wrong on purpose, and it is the most useful sentence a patient can say.

triage.guide.syringes.body:
Everything else in the bag is something you do with your hands over a minute. These are decisions made in a second, and every one of them can be the wrong decision.

Adrenaline has two right uses. In a stopped heart it does not restart anything - nothing in a needle restarts a heart - it makes the next round of compressions worth what the first one was, which is exactly what it is given between cycles for. And it is the only answer to a body destroying the blood that was hung on it.

Its wrong use looks exactly like its right one, and that is what makes it the most dangerous thing here. Somebody emptying out looks like somebody fading, and the instinct is to push something into them. Adrenaline raises the pressure, and in a body with an open vessel that means the bleed pours: every light one turns heavy and the volume goes while you are still feeling useful. Two shots on top of each other is the other way a heart stops.

Morphine is the opposite of the pills: at once, strong, works on somebody already on the floor, and it does not care how many courses they have had because it is not the same drug. What it costs is the drive to breathe. On a chest that is already failing - crushed, broken, full of something - it can stop them breathing altogether. They go down, the airway clock starts, and a pair of hands answers it.

So does the third needle. Naloxone undoes morphine and nothing else, and on somebody whose breathing has gone it is the difference between a patient and a body. Pushed into somebody who was being held together by the dose it does exactly what it says: takes the morphine away, all of it, at once - and what arrives instead is every bit of what was being kept off them.

triage.guide.sleepless.body:
The game has always counted how long since you slept, and has always done one thing with it: send birds. That is a threat from outside. What being awake for three days actually does is from the inside, and it is the best documented thing in this book.

A tired pair of hands is a worse pair of hands, and the person they belong to is the last to know it. So this is the fifth thing that decides a treatment, after the room, the instrument, the second pair of hands, and what this pair has just been carrying. It is the only one of the five with no answer available in the next half minute.

It costs two other things and both are real. A body that has not slept catches what is going around, and a wound on a sleepless body takes longer to knit, because knitting is mostly a thing a body does while it is asleep.

And you can see it. Past the first day the lids come down, and they come down further the longer it goes on; the blinks get slower and the gaps between them get shorter. At the far end one of those blinks stops being a blink - the world goes away for a second and a half and comes back with you somewhere else, which is what happens to people who drive tired. It chooses the moment, not you.

The first day is free: one night up is not a medical fact. After that it climbs, and there is exactly one way out of it, and it is the one the game has always had.

triage.guide.thermometer: The one number nobody can feel
triage.guide.thermometer.body:
You can tell by touch that a forehead is hot. You cannot tell by touch that it is thirty-eight point six, and the difference between those two sentences is an instrument.

Mercury does not go back on its own - that is the whole trick of it, and it is why a thermometer opens showing somebody else's temperature. Shake it down before you use it or you will read the last one.

It goes into a fold of skin and stays there: a body breathes, the fold moves, and a thermometer out of the fold gathers nothing. The column climbs fast, then slower, then hardly at all, and the whole skill is knowing it has stopped.

And then it has to be read. The column is a hair of metal behind a lens of glass; turn it in the light until the thread flashes against the scale.
triage.msg.not_bacterial: A course does nothing against this. It is not bacteria
triage.guide.virus.body:
Everything a course of antibiotics answers in this mod is bacterial, and until there was something else the mod never had to say so.

A virus is not a stronger illness. It is a different kind of thing, and a course poured into one achieves nothing whatever except that the course is gone - which is worth knowing before you spend the last bottle on somebody who was going to get better anyway, and worth knowing before you do not spend one on somebody who was not.

Influenza runs hot and spreads off a sneeze the way a cold does. It comes from where influenza actually comes from, which is a crowd: stand about in a village long enough and somebody in it was ill. It passes on its own given time and somewhere warm, and most of the time that is all it does.

What it can do on the way is leave a chest open to pneumonia - which is how influenza has always killed people, and which is the one part of it a bottle does answer. Whether it does is decided by the body: cold, wet or three days awake and the chest is likely to open, dry and warm and rested and it will not open at all. So the course is not useless; it is simply for the complication and not for the virus.

The stomach one comes off what was eaten, and it empties people rather than burning them. It has no cure and it does not need one: what it needs is fluid, faster than it is going out. That is a reason to reach for a bag of saline that is not a wound, and there was not one before.

And the forehead is how you tell. A virus and an infected wound both run hot, and only one of them is worth a bottle.

triage.guide.feel.body:
A bone that has moved out of line can be seen from across a room. A bone that broke and stayed where it was shows nothing at all, and there are exactly two ways to find one: a film, or a hand.

Press in three places, firmly enough to be on bone and no harder. Too light and you are feeling skin. Too hard and you hurt them for nothing - and on a break that is still fresh, a press like that moves it, which turns a bone that would have healed straight into one that has to be pulled back into line first.

On yourself it is worth less. Your own hand stops early, every time, and that is not cowardice.

triage.guide.listen.title: Listening to a chest
triage.guide.listen.body:
A chest is the one part of somebody that says nothing from the outside. A lung that has come away from the wall looks exactly like a lung that has not, and what the patient tells you - that they cannot breathe - is the same sentence they say with a mouthful of blood.

So it is the only finding here with no free way in, and that is what the instrument is for.

Four places, a second at each, and hold the bell still: a bell that slides on skin is a bell listening to your own hand. What you are listening for is a difference between the two sides. Air on both is the answer you want. Air on one is a needle, now.

triage.command.realistic: Difficulty: realistic — the chart is what somebody found out.
triage.guide.difficulty.title: Two difficulties
triage.guide.difficulty.body:
Arcade is this mod as it has always been: the chart is a readout. Open it and it tells you the left leg has two breaks and an infection.

Realistic changes one thing - where that knowledge comes from. Same injuries, same treatments, same games. What goes is the free answer: a part nobody has examined reads as a blank, and the difference between 'nothing there' and 'did not look' is the whole of it.

What anybody in the room can see stays visible in both: blood, a missing limb, a burn, a bone through the skin, a leg lying at an angle it does not bend at. What is inside somebody has to be found - by hand, by instrument, or by asking them while they can still answer.

The server decides which, in the config. Two people in one world cannot be playing two different games.

triage.guide.survey.title: Looking somebody over
triage.guide.survey.body:
The first thing anybody does to anybody, and it answers *where* rather than *what*.

One pass down the body tells you how bad each part is - which is what looking at somebody tells you in life. It does not tell you why: a leg that is in a bad way could be a break, a bleed, a burn under the cloth or a limb that died under a strap, and finding out which is what the hands and the instruments are for.

Which is exactly why it is worth doing first. Without it, examining somebody properly means feeling along seven parts in turn, and nobody has four minutes for that with a person bleeding in front of them. One sweep turns seven questions into one.

Keep pace with the band. Hurry and your hands go past the quiet leg - the one nobody is complaining about, which in this mod as in life is the one that kills them an hour later.

triage.guide.tetanus.body:
The only thing in this mod that cares what shape a wound is. A gash that goes bad goes septic; a deep narrow hole - an arrow, a fragment - closed at the top with the bottom still sealed in does something else, and it starts silently.

While it is silent it is treatable, and nothing tells you it is there. The one tell is a sentence: ask them, and a patient with a stiffening jaw says so.

When the silence ends the course stops working and the spasms start - and a spasm is the only thing here that interrupts a treatment from the inside. Somebody nobody can finish working on is a problem with no answer left.

The way to not have it: take the metal out and wash the hole before anything goes over it.
triage.guide.crush.body:
A limb with nothing going through it fills up with everything a living limb flushes away. Release the strap and all of it arrives at the heart at once.

Which is not an argument for leaving the strap on - that kills the limb - and not for taking it off quickly either. It is an argument for **fluid first**: a patient who is not short of blood takes what comes back out of that leg diluted, and nothing happens. A patient already down on volume takes it neat, and the answer is the same bag, hung too late.

The clock is the one that was already running: the longer the strap has been killing the limb, the worse the release.
triage.guide.relapse.body:
One bottle is one dose, and a dose is not a course. Sometimes the fever lifts, the patient gets up, and it is back in waves a few minutes later.

What makes it worth knowing is what it does to the thermometer. A fever that cycles is **normal at the bottom of its cycle** - so a reading taken then is honest, accurate and says there is nothing wrong. Nothing else in this mod can be right and wrong at the same time.

Measure twice, ten seconds apart. That is the whole trick, and it is the trick in life too.

triage.guide.blade.body:
Rarely, a blade heavy enough to have gone in deep stays in - and whoever swung it does not have it any more. It is the only disarm in this mod and it happens to the winner of the fight.

While it is in, it is **holding the wound shut**. That is not a figure of speech: the wound it made is not bleeding because the thing that made it is still in the hole. Nothing can be bandaged over it, nothing clots around it, and the part will not mend while it is there.

So taking it out is the injury, and there are two ways.

**Bare hands** are always available, take no kit, and leave the worst bleed in the mod behind them - or, if the hands were steady, only a heavy one. **Forceps and a kit** leave a bleed a dressing answers.

That is the whole decision, and it is asked at the worst possible moment every time: now with hands, or in a minute with a kit. In between, every step they take moves it.

triage.guide.earshot.body:
A chest in trouble is loud, and it is loud to anybody in the room before an instrument is out of a bag. Kneel next to somebody and you can hear whether their chest is working.

What you hear is only **that** something is wrong - never the rate, never the cause. A wet chest, a chest that cannot finish a breath, and a chest working far too hard sound different from each other and from nothing at all. The stethoscope stops being how you find out a chest is bad and becomes how you find out which bad it is, which is what a stethoscope is for.

The worst one makes no sound. That is not a gap in the mod: a chest that has stopped is silent, and somebody who has learned to listen for the noise will one day notice it missing.
triage.guide.panic.body:
Until now the only thing that could stop an operation was somebody hitting the person doing it. The patient - awake, with nothing in them, with a saw against their leg - held perfectly still, because nobody had ever written the line that says people in agony do not.

Now they pull away. Only on jobs that open skin, and scaled by how much pain they are actually in.

There are three answers and the mod already had all three: **ether**, which takes the person away from the room; **painkillers**, which take the pain down far enough that they can bear it; and **a second pair of hands**, which costs nothing but a friend crouching beside you with an empty hand. Any one of them and this never happens.

Nothing is spent when they pull away. What it costs is the time, and the walk back for whichever of those three you did not bother with.

triage.obs.hint: Two readings make a direction. One makes a number.
triage.guide.obs.body:
One measurement is not information. Two are.

Every reading anybody takes off a body now goes on a sheet, with the time on it and the name of whoever took it. Open it from the chart - the three lines in the top corner.

A pulse of 112 means nothing on its own. A pulse of 112 on somebody who was at 90 four minutes ago is bleeding somewhere, and there is no wound on the outside to find. **That is what the second reading buys**, and it is the only finding in this mod whose price is patience rather than an item.

The chart prints an arrow beside a reading once there is something to compare it with, and the mod says the arithmetic out loud when you take it - never what it means. A climbing pulse is also a frightened person, a running person, and a fever on its way up. Which one it is, is your job.

And a patient lying beside a medical table is written up automatically, every so often, by nobody. That is what a clinic is for, and it is the first reason in this mod to carry somebody somewhere.
